what: A test Subject staged in real time for the late-correction case. Revision 1 was in force from 2026-11-25T18:30Z. An agent-side record referencing revision 1 was anchored by its operator in Bitcoin block 977556 (mined 2026-11-25T19:12:23Z). Revision 2 (with source_revision) was issued only after that, so the anchor is earlier than the correction in fact and not by construction.

expected.note: What a verifier can establish, by observation. The earliest issuance time of revision 2 is left unresolved: the evidence gives an upper bound and a publisher-declared earlier view, not proof of absence. (Form suggested on the SCITT list, 2026-11-26.)
established: revision 1 was listed as the only revision in two signed, logged publisher views, one before and one after the anchor
the receipt referencing revision 1 existed by 2026-11-25T19:12:23Z
not_established: the earliest time revision 2 was issued: the publisher states 2026-11-26T02:33:42Z; nothing outside the publisher shows it

that revision 2 did not exist when sequence 3 was signed: sequence 3 is the publisher's own declaration of completeness for this Subject (the list states it holds every digest issued), so it commits the publisher to that view and would expose a contradiction, but it is not proof of absence
expected.earlier_views: Each sequence is the file at https://financeratecalc.com/transparency/statement-digests.json as it stood then; retrieve it from the repository history and compare its SHA-256 with list_sha256 and with previous_sha256 in the next sequence.
